description: I am a digital circuit designer interested in space, seeking to expand my expertise into aerospace engineering.
summary:
OmniMars is an integrated mission planning and navigation platform designed to streamline Martian exploration from orbital reconnaissance to  Extravehicular Activity (EVA) execution.

Current planetary tools often fragment global terrain analysis from localized environmental simulation.OmniMars bridges this gap through a dual-mode architecture.

Mission Planning Mode combines multi-layer orbital datasets, solar illumination modeling, and spatial measurement tools to evaluate candidate landing zones and compile scientific waypoints.

EVA Mode transitions to site-locked, high-resolution operations—demonstrated at Jezero Crater—integrating HiRISE/DTM terrain, localized atmospheric modeling, historical rover traverses, and precision surface routing. By unifying high-resolution geospatial data with dynamic environmental constraints, OmniMars enables mission planners and astronauts to mitigate terrain and weather hazards, ensuring safer, data-driven, and efficient operations for future human and robotic Mars missions.
details:
What does it do?

Built on CesiumJS, this project implements an interactive web platform that enables users to conduct simulations and mission planning through various web-based tools, featuring two modes:

  • Mission Planning Mode: Supports both 3D and 2D global views, allowing users to identify scientific sites of interest or candidate landing zones for future crewed missions by integrating and overlaying Mars Trek layers. Additionally, this mode provides convenient and efficient tools for early-stage mission planning, including measuring distances and elevation, simulating solar lighting and shadows while calculating elevation and azimuth angles, and adding custom markers.
  • EVA Mode: Provides Extravehicular Activity (EVA) assessment and navigation assistance for specific sites, demonstrated using Jezero Crater. In this mode, users can further integrate high-resolution HiRISE imagery to clearly identify obstacles and elevation changes, while utilizing the Mars Climate Database (MCD) model to compute local environmental conditions as key evaluation metrics for EVA operations. For surface navigation, the system performs preliminary grid discretization and incorporates geological and elevation maps as traversal cost factors—accounting for terrain slope and potential sinkage on overly soft surfaces—to automatically plan routes between two points and calculate total distance and climb gradient.

What benefits does it have?

By integrating multiple existing tools and scientific datasets alongside convenient built-in utilities, OmniMars reduces the complexity researchers face during mission planning. Furthermore, it delivers localized EVA navigation capabilities that existing platforms do not account for.

What is the intended impact of the project?

In light of NASA's future crewed Moon to Mars program, existing tools remain overly fragmented and rely on cumbersome data without offering a convenient, integrated solution. By combining two core modes, this project delivers an end-to-end workflow spanning macro-level mission planning to practical EVA navigation, aiming to serve as a prototype for future mission planning tools and procedures.

 What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • React / Next.js: Acts as the core front-end framework, leveraging its efficient component-based architecture and dual-mode interface design (supporting SSR/CSR dynamic loading).
  • JavaScript / TypeScript: Used to implement front-end interactive logic, UI state management, and algorithms.
  • HTML5 / CSS3 / Tailwind CSS: Used to build sci-fi themed (HUD-style) user interfaces and layouts.
  • CesiumJS: The core 3D geospatial visualization engine. Used for rendering the global 3D Mars globe, terrain, multi-layered orbital data layers, billboards, and camera view transitions.
  • Vercel: Used for cloud-based automated deployment and web hosting.
  • Git / GitHub: Version control and collaboration tools.
  • Cursor: Coding IDE

How is your project creative? &  What factors did your team consider?

The innovation and core considerations of this project lie in integrating the Mars Climate Database (MCD) model, calculating solar elevation and azimuth angles, and leveraging elevation and geological maps to simulate real-world environmental conditions as accurately as possible for navigation and site selection. To further emulate real astronaut mission scenarios, oxygen consumption metrics—derived from the Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document—have also been integrated into the navigation system.
